title: Memory Decoder at Scale — code view
subtitle: What the LUMIA-Group/MemoryDecoder-at-Scale repo actually executes. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); empty lanes do not exist in this system.
source: repo MemoryDecoder-at-Scale @ bbbfee85 ("Initial release")   ·   verified against servers/memorydecoder/verification.md (61 code-side assertions: 43 ✓ / 2 ✗ / 16 ◐)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · code view · every citation re-opened and confirmed during verification
legend_notes: Same 6-lane footprint as the paper: A1, A4, A5, A6, B6, B7 have content; B1-B5 are genuinely empty — the whole self-query/index/distribution machinery in A4 runs once while building the datastore, not at query time.

Two of the paper's mechanism claims do not survive contact with the code: the distributed OPQ+HNSW+sharded Faiss pipeline is a single-machine IndexIVFPQ with no OPQ, no HNSW and no sharding (each process just loads the whole index onto its own GPU), and --ignore_first unconditionally drops the nearest neighbor regardless of whether it equals the query, silently cutting the effective neighbor count from K=1024 to 1023. See the diff view for the full paper⇄code contrast.

λ selection is genuinely THREE independently-written implementations, not the two-way split some docs describe: only the general-suite launcher uses the 288-entry task-aware auto-table; FinEval's own launcher and the standalone knowledge-task scripts (multihopqa, halueval) hardcode 0.3 and bypass the registry entirely; OpenCompass (BioInst/LawBench) is a third, separately hardcoded 0.3 default.

The domain-memory continued-pretraining step the paper requires (§3.3) has no launcher anywhere in scripts/ — drawn here as paper_only. A fully working classic online kNN-LM interpolator (KNNWrapperMulti) also ships in the repo with zero reachable call sites; see the diff view rather than this one, since it never actually executes.
